comments.body:
Landed as Gerrit change 3109 (commit ae02e364465, LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, 0 unresolved).

Measured before the fix: a bounded ticket-create git commit takes about 0.025 s on this host, so the 1.0 s kill bound had large headroom on a healthy commit. A git shim that sleeps 1.3 s before commit, with no repack involved, reproduces exactly the reported 'git timed out after 1.0s'. So the old test failed on any slow commit, whatever the cause.

The test now sets GIT_TRACE2_EVENT and asserts the structural invariant instead: with the _AUTOMAINT_OFF suppression in place, no maintenance, gc, repack, pack-objects or multi-pack-index process is a descendant of a git commit process. The 1.0 s _GIT_TIMEOUT patch is gone and production keeps its 30 s default. A detector test empties _AUTOMAINT_OFF and must find 'maintenance run --auto' under the commit.

Scratch checks: the invariant test fails with _AUTOMAINT_OFF emptied, and passes with every git commit delayed 1.3 s.

Unverified: the original failing run had no trace, so the exact slow step in that run is unknown. The fix removes the dependence on wall-clock time; it does not identify what stalled that commit.

compiled_state.description:
## Observation
During the comment-remediation Group17 full `make verify` run on macOS/Git 2.56, `tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py::test_write_survives_foreground_maintenance_repack` failed because the ticket-create `git commit` exceeded its monkeypatched `_GIT_TIMEOUT=1.0`. The same unchanged test passed in 163.96 seconds isolated and again in 44.00 seconds with Git Trace2 under concurrent suites; the latter measured both ticket-create commits at 0.015 seconds each. The Group17 patch changes only comments in other files and preserves normalized AST. At the check, host load averages were 18.13/21.83/22.56, but the failed run has no Git trace, so the cause is unproven.

## Measurements (2026-10-25, this host, real git, same 20,000-loose-object fixture)
- The bounded `git commit` took 0.025 s and 0.019 s at host load 8 to 13; the explicit separate maintenance step took 6.5 s on its first run and 0.015 s on the second (its bound is 120 s). So the 1.0 s kill bound has about 40x headroom on a healthy commit.
- A git shim that sleeps 1.3 s before `commit` (no repack involved) fails the test with exactly the reported "git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out after 1.0s". Any commit slower than 1 s fails it, whatever it is doing.
- Git Trace2 (`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`) shows the real structural difference. With the suppression in place, no `maintenance`, `gc` or `repack` process is a descendant of the `git commit` process; the explicit step is a separate top-level `git maintenance run --auto` and owns the repack. With the original defect (`_AUTOMAINT_OFF` emptied), `git maintenance run --auto` is a CHILD of `git commit`, and `repack`, `pack-objects` and `multi-pack-index` hang below it. A flat search for any repack is wrong: the fixed flow also runs them, under the separate step.

## Root cause
The test uses a wall-clock kill bound (1.0 s) as a proxy for the invariant "auto-maintenance does not run inside the bounded commit". The bound is valid only while a healthy commit stays under it; host starvation can break that without any maintenance running. Not reproduced: the original single failure under load (the failed run had no Git trace), so the exact slow step there is unknown.

## Approach
1. In `tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py`, stop patching `_GIT_TIMEOUT` to 1.0 and keep the production 30 s default.
2. Set `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` to a file via `monkeypatch.setenv` and run the two creates.
3. Parse the trace with a helper: collect the sids of top-level `commit` processes (a sid with no `/`, argv containing `commit`), then report every process whose sid starts with one of those sids plus `/` and whose command is `maintenance`, `gc`, `repack`, `pack-objects` or `multi-pack-index`.
4. Assert at least one `commit` process was traced (so an empty trace cannot pass), that no maintenance descendant exists, and that both creates return ids.
5. Add a detector test with the suppression removed (`event_commit_git._AUTOMAINT_OFF` set to `()`): the same helper must now find a maintenance descendant of a commit. This replaces the proof the 1 s bound used to give.

## Scope
In scope: `tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py`. Out of scope: production code, `_GIT_TIMEOUT`, the explicit maintenance step, and its 120 s bound.

## Testing
```
pytest tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py -q
make verify
```
Also run the new test with a git shim that sleeps 1.3 s before `commit` (it must still pass, since no kill bound is involved). Failure case: with `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` emptied the new maintenance-descendant assertion fails, deterministically, with no dependence on timing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The test fails when the suppression is removed and passes with it, without relying on a wall-clock bound (checked: detector test, and a seeded run with `_AUTOMAINT_OFF` emptied).
- [x] The test passes when every `git commit` is delayed 1.3 s (checked: shim run recorded in a ticket comment).
- [x] The commit-maintenance invariant is still asserted: no maintenance, gc or repack descendant of a commit (checked: the test body).
- [x] `make verify` is green on the Linux CI gate (`Verified +1` on the Gerrit change).

file_impact.reason: Assert the structural no-maintenance-in-commit invariant via Trace2 instead of a load-sensitive 1 s kill bound
